subject.title: fix: prioritize exhausted Antigravity quota in menu bar and highest usage

question: Should Antigravity automatic selection use context-specific semantics—reset-oriented selection for reset text and a shared binding lane for percentage, pace, and highest usage—or should one global lane-selection rule govern every display mode?
rationale: The shared resolver serves different user intents, and neither source behavior nor tests establish whether reset urgency or actionable quota pressure should take precedence across all modes.

options.title: Use context-specific selection
options.body: Select by reset relevance for reset-focused text, but use one binding quota lane consistently for percentage, pace, provider ranking, and rendered highest-usage text.

options.title: Use one constrained-lane rule
options.body: Always select the most binding supported quota lane and use reset time only as a tie-breaker across all automatic modes.

options.title: Preserve usable-lane behavior
options.body: Continue suppressing exhausted lanes whenever another lane remains usable, accepting that reset-focused text will not surface the blocked quota.

recommendation.title: Use context-specific selection
recommendation.body: Select by reset relevance for reset-focused text, but use one binding quota lane consistently for percentage, pace, provider ranking, and rendered highest-usage text.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice defines repository-wide menu-bar product semantics rather than a mechanical implementation detail.
